div.head: Af 1.2
div.ab: [Gif he þonne þæs weddige þe him riht sie to gelæstanne] ⁊ þæt aleoge, selle mid eaðmedum his wæpn ⁊ his æhta his freondum to gehealdanne ⁊ beo feowertig nihta on carcerne on cyninges tune, ðrowige ðær swa biscep him scrife, ⁊ his mægas hine feden, gif he self mete næbbe.

Gif he þonne ðæs weddie þe hym riht sy to gelæstanne ⁊ þæt aleoge, sylle mid eadmedum hys wæpn ⁊ his æhta his freondum to gehealdenne ⁊ beo XL nihta on carcerne æt cyninges tune, þrowie ðær swa biscop him scrife, ⁊ his magas hine fedan, gif he sylf mete næbbe.

Si quis autem hoc uadiet quod fieri iustum sit, et transgrediatur, committat arma sua et pecuniam amicis suis in custodiam et sit XL noctibus in carcere ad mansionem regiam et peniteat ibi secundum iussionem episcopi sui, et parentes eius pascant eum, si ipse uictum non habeat.

[Gif he þonne þæs weddige þe him riht sie to gelæstanne] ⁊ þæt aleoge, selle mid eaðmedum his wæpn ⁊ his æhta his freondum to gehealdanne ⁊ beo feowertig nihta on carcerne on cyninges tune, ðrowige ðær swa biscep him scrife, ⁊ his mægas hine feden, gif he self mete næbbe.

[Gif he þonne þæs weddie þe hym riht sy to gelæstanne] [H] ⁊ þæt aleoge, selle mid eaðmedum his wæpn ⁊ his æhta his freondum to gehealdanne ⁊ beo feowertig nihta on carcene on cyninges tune; ðrowige ðær swa biscep him scrife, ⁊ his mægas hine feden, gif he self mete næbbe.

Wenn er jedoch zu solchem sich verpflichtet, was zu leisten für ihn rechtmässig ist, und dies nicht erfüllt, so gebe er mit Demuth seine Waffen und seine Habe seinen Freunden zu verwahren und sei 40 Nächte im Kerker in einer Ortschaft des Königs, dulde dort, wie der Bischof ihm zur Busse auferlegt; und seine Verwandten sollen ihn ernähren, wenn er selbst keinen Unterhalt hat.

But if he pledges himself to something which it is lawful for him to perform, and does not fulfil it, then let him with humility give his weapons and his property to his friends to keep, and be 40 nights in prison in a royal township, and undergo there what the bishop imposes on him as penance; and his kinsmen are to feed him if he himself has no sustenance.

If, however, he pledges himself to something which it is lawful to carry out and proves false to his pledge, he shall humbly give his weapons and possessions to his friends to keep, and remain 40 days in prison at a royal manor, and undergo there whatever [sentence] the bishop prescribes for him; and his relatives shall feed him if he himself has no food.

[If, however, he pledges what it is right for him to perform,] and leaves it unfulfilled, let him with humility give his weapons and his possessions into his friends’ keeping and be 40 days in prison at a king’s estate; let him endure there what penance the bishop prescribes for him, and his kinsmen are to feed him if he has no food himself.

[If he should, however, pledge himself to that which it is right for him to perform] and [subsequently] repudiate it, let him humbly give his weapons and his possessions to his friend-group to hold, and let him be in the prison on an estate of the king for forty nights, and there undergo [penance?] in accordance with what the bishop prescribes, and let his kinsman feed him, if he himself has no food.

‘zu leisten hat (Schmid 657b) dem Herrn’. Gemeint ist, was er darf, im Ggs. zu den Fällen 1, 1
‘has to perform (Schmid 657b) for the lord’. What is meant is what he is permitted to do, in contrast to the cases of 1, 1

Vgl. Gl Sippe 16e. Wie weit sich der Kreis der Blutsfreunde erstreckte, erhellt nicht. Aber ‘immediate family’ allein ist nicht (mit Phillpott Kindred 213) darunter zu verstehen möglich: dáfür hätte Af eines der Wörter für ‘Haushalt’ verwendet

Cf. Gl Sippe 16e. How far the circle of blood-relatives extended is not clear. But it is not possible (with Phillpott Kindred 213) to understand by it the ‘immediate family’ alone: for that Af would have used one of the words for ‘household’

Vgl. Gl Gefängnis. Das Wort begegnet nicht etwa bei Af zuerst. — 40 und 120 Tage Gefängnis s. Gl Frist 14b. 17. Ælfred in Augustin (ed. Hargrove 44) beschreibt, wer alles im Königshofe lebt: sume on bure, sume on healle, sume on odne, sume on carcerne; and hy lybbað þeah æalle be anes hlafordes are. Also in jedem Königsheim stellt er sich ein Gefängnis vor

Cf. Gl Gefängnis. It is not in Af, say, that the word first occurs. — For 40 and 120 days’ imprisonment see Gl Frist 14b. 17. Ælfred in his Augustine (ed. Hargrove 44) describes all those who live at the king’s court: sume on bure, sume on healle, sume on odne, sume on carcerne; and hy lybbað þeah æalle be anes hlafordes are. So he pictures a prison in every royal residence
Der Schreiber H missversteht vielleicht ‘zu Kingston’ [upon Thames]. Gemeint ist Königsdomäne; s. d. Gl
The scribe of H perhaps misunderstands it as ‘at Kingston’ [upon Thames]. Royal demesne is meant; see that word in Gl

nicht ‘tue Busse’ (Q, Schmid) in rein kirchlicher Bed. Der unter religiöser Einwirkung entstandene German. Formalkontrakt ward, früher als durch den Staat, durch die Kirche, die den Bruch der fides facta strafte (u. 1, 8), in Schutz genommen; Pol Mai II 184. 187. 189. (Mit dem foreað [s. Gl Klageeid] vermengt dies irrig Price.) Vgl. Gl Versprechen 6; Geistliches Gericht 14a. — Der Anordner der Strafe war regelmässig der Diözesan des Schuldigen; daher ist sui in Q zumeist, doch vielleicht nicht immer (wenn dieser z. B. ausserhalb der Heimat belangt war) richtig. Unten 1, 8 his scrift ist der Bischof oder dessen Vertreter, der Pfarrer

not ‘do penance’ (Q, Schmid) in a purely ecclesiastical sense. The Germanic formal contract, which arose under religious influence, was taken under protection by the Church, which punished breach of the fides facta (below 1, 8), earlier than by the State; Pol Mai II 184. 187. 189. (Price wrongly confuses this with the foreað [see Gl Klageeid].) Cf. Gl Versprechen 6; Geistliches Gericht 14a. — The authority who imposed the penalty was as a rule the culprit’s diocesan; hence sui in Q is right in most cases, though perhaps not always (e.g. if he had been proceeded against away from home). Below, 1, 8, his scrift is the bishop or his representative, the parish priest
Hunger erschwert sonst Gefängnis (s. d. 6) und Asyl; s. d. Gl 9
Elsewhere hunger is used to make imprisonment (see that word 6) and sanctuary harsher; see that word in Gl 9
[ändere so erste Anm.-Zahl 4]. Vgl. Gl Waffe 4
[change the first note number 4 to this]. Cf. Gl Waffe 4
This is perhaps the most satisfactory translation of the expression cyninges tun. (Quadr. translates ad mansionem regiam.) The usual meaning of tun is ‘village.’
This and the next clause are from Exodus xxiii. 1, 2.
